correctness.rationale: For the N-point metric with only adjacent d(a,b)=r and d(b,c)=s shorter than one, 0<r,s<1,r+s≥1, vertices of the dual Lipschitz polytope are exactly connected tight-edge configurations. Every outsider must take one of two binary values; the special (a,b,c)-triple has 16 feasible connected-tight templates in the generic chamber. Counting 10 all-zero outsider, 10 all-one outsider and 16 for every mixed binary outsider assignment yields 2^(N+1)-12. On r=s or r+s=1, exact independent coalescences of candidate triples yield counts 7·2^(N−2)−10 and 7·2^(N−2)−12, and 3·2^(N−1)−10 at their intersection. A vertex at a boundary is a limit of maximizing vertices from the adjacent chamber, so no new templates appear. Fresh exact rational active-halfspace enumeration independent of the template recovered N=4 counts 20,18,16,14 and N=5 counts 52,46,44,38. This is finite corroboration; the tight-graph proof is all-N.
